author: val
body: THE ROWS SPAN 80 DEGREES NORTH TO 60 SOUTH, which is where a real Mercator stops being usable: the projection sends the poles to infinity, so every published one is cropped and this one is cropped in the same place. It costs nothing, because nobody picks a timezone by clicking Antarctica.

author: val
body: Each row is 144 bits as nine 16-bit words, most significant bit first, which is the shape that fits an Integer literal per word and stays readable as a map when the words are laid out in a column. Sea is 0 and land is 1.

author: val
body: THE BAND IS THE COLUMN AND THE COLUMN IS THE LONGITUDE. 144 columns over 360 degrees is six columns per hour, and the map is centred so that column 72 is the prime meridian: stripe s spans columns `72 + s * 6` to `72 + s * 6 + 6`.

author: val
body: Stripes run -12 to +11 across the picture, which is 24 bands and covers the world once. The table has zones at +12, +13 and +14, which are east of the date line and are drawn in the SAME columns as -12, -11 and -10. That is not a bug in the picture, it is what the date line is, and the list beside the map is what separates them.

author: val
body: GENERATED, and the generator is not in the depot because its OUTPUT is the artifact: 367 non-empty words rasterised from about twenty coastline polygons in latitude and longitude. Editing a coastline here means editing these numbers, which is the honest cost of a picture in a language with no array literal, and the picture is checked by looking at it rather than by reading them.
